page: The Vultr vc2-16c-64gb is a Cloud Compute virtual instance built on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 16 virtual CPUs derived from 8 physical cores on an Intel Xeon processor running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU allocation is shared across host hardware. The processor configuration includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 4 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache, with hardware support for AVX, AVX-512F, AES, and BMI2 instruction sets. It includes 64 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4 GB per virtual core. Storage is provisioned locally as a 1280 GB NVMe SSD, and networking includes one complimentary public IPv4 address without dedicated GPU acceleration.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-tier throughput across parallelized computing tasks alongside notable single-threaded constraints. Multi-core performance reaches middle-tier levels across synthetic suites, with a multi-core Geekbench score of 6565.0, a PassMark CPU rating of 21511.0, and stress-ng multi-core throughput of 21535.52. In contrast, single-thread processing exhibits limitations attributable to the 2.0 GHz shared clock frequency, recording a single-core Geekbench score of 836.0 and text processing performance in the bottom 10 percent. Large-block memory transfers achieve 107.12 GB/sec read and 53.71 GB/sec write bandwidth, while cached small-block reads measure 1518.77 GB/sec. Application testing demonstrates 23.04 million Redis SET operations per second and 12.01 GB/sec static web throughput.

Cost efficiency is driven by the density of paired resources, combining a substantial 64 GB memory footprint and 1280 GB NVMe storage on a shared compute tier. The primary architectural tradeoff lies between abundant multi-threaded capacity and lower single-thread instruction throughput. This server profile is appropriate for scale-out web serving, multi-threaded continuous integration builds, caching layers, and database workloads requiring high local disk capacity and memory rather than peak single-core clock frequencies.
description: Vultr vc2-16c-64gb is a Cloud Compute virtual server featuring 16 shared vCPUs on an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz across 8 physical cores. The instance is configured with 64 GB of system RAM, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, and includes 1280 GB of local NVMe SSD storage without discrete GPU hardware. Benchmark metrics reveal solid multi-core performance, evidenced by a PassMark CPU score of 21511.0 and a multi-core Geekbench rating of 6565.0, balanced against lower single-thread execution speeds. Memory performance delivers up to 107.12 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth, with application throughput reaching 23.04 million Redis SET operations per second and 12.01 GB/sec in static web serving. The balanced resource configuration and fast local storage make this instance suitable for container hosts, database nodes, caching deployments, and multi-threaded compilation tasks.
